summary: The draft is disciplined about keeping β.G5 open, explicitly warns against the earlier Prop. 19.2 cross-space misuse, and its high-level read of Approaches A/C plus the scoped §3.1/§3.2 takeaways is mostly honest. However, it is not yet clean enough to pass: the citation taxonomy is applied inconsistently at first mention of non-verified sources, and Approach D still overstates a "partial progress" reduction by collapsing an adaptive adversarial strategy class to a single-round fixed-channel REE expression without a supporting theorem.

issues.description: Approach D claims possible 'partial progress' via a bound of the form `sup_Π R <= sup_M E_R(\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_M)`, but the preceding discussion only establishes at most a purification/indexing of adaptive strategies by Eve's initial memory. That does not justify collapsing a full adaptive comb or strategy family to a single-round fixed-channel amortized REE expression. This risks reintroducing a softer version of the same scope jump the draft is trying to avoid.
issues.suggestion: Remove the displayed 'partial progress' claim or weaken it to: purification may at best parameterize a family of adversarial combs/channels by an initial Eve register, but no single fixed-channel amortization bound follows without a new theorem handling strategy families or memory channels.

issues.description: The document's own five-level citation taxonomy is not applied consistently on first mention of non-verified literature. `Pirandola 2017` is cited in the Approach B header/body without an explicit `[RECALLED]` tag, and `Kamin 2025 / Metger 2024` are introduced in Approach C before the qualifier appears only on subordinate claims. Given the draft's explicit taxonomy policy, this is a citation-discipline failure.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit taxonomy labels at first mention of each external source in Approaches B/C, e.g. `Approach B — Teleportation stretching [Pirandola 2017, RECALLED]` and `Approach C — Kamin 2025 / Metger 2024 GEAT [RECALLED]`, then keep any finer-grained caveats inside the section.

round_recommendation: Retag all non-verified citations at first mention and rewrite Approach D so it states only the negative conclusion (worst-case purification does not yield a fixed-channel amortization theorem) without any unsupported partial-bound formula.
